summary: Persistent keepalive/telemetry heartbeats from ingestion worker exhausting burst credits and causing 429s during low-traffic windows
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses that appear only during their low-traffic windows (nightly maintenance window) despite overall low token usage. Problem correlates with a newly-deployed ingestion agent that emits persistent keepalive telemetry pings (HTTP/WS) every 30s from ~200 worker processes. Impact:
- Multiple endpoints returning 429s for the tenant for 10-40 minutes during a daily window (~02:00-03:00 US-EAST).
- Affects live inference calls and some scheduled batch jobs; customer observed tail-latency regressions and dropped requests.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated GPU pool), us-east region, Prod
- Ingestion agents running in customer's VPC with an outbound NAT/edge proxy in front of Redwood edge.
Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Deploy 150-250 ingestion workers configured to open one persistent websocket to our streaming API and send a telemetry heartbeat JSON every 30s.
2) At low application traffic (few real calls), observe rate-limit headers returned on subsequent requests.
3) After ~5–10 minutes, tenant-level 429s rise sharply until burst credits recover.
Observed behavior:
- X-RateLimit-Remaining drops rapidly despite low nominal request volume.
- X-RateLimit-Reset indicates refill windows misaligned with expected cadence.
- 429s are tenant-scoped (all routes for the tenant) and disproportionately occur only during nightly window.
Expected behavior:
- Keepalives / telemetry pings should not consume tenant burst credits in a way that causes customer-facing 429s during low-traffic windows.
Attachments: logs, headers, small sequence diagram customer included.
logs: Sample throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-10T02:10:00Z
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Support):
- Verified customer timestamps against our ratecontrol metrics; tenant burst credits show repeated small drains that align with telemetry heartbeat schedule.
- Confirmed edge-proxy/NAT reuse: customer uses pooled outbound IPs; 200 worker websockets appear to be multiplexed over a small set of NAT mappings.
SRE hypothesis: telemetry keepalive requests (and their preflight/health probes) are being counted as full quota-bearing requests and producing per-request token consumption. Because heartbeats are synchronous and aligned (every 30s), they create a sawtooth that exhausts burst credits in the refill window.
Additional findings:
- Some telemetry endpoints use the same route as inference calls (/v1/streams) which does not have an internal-exempt tag.
- Edge-proxy logs show multiple socket reconnects from the same NAT mapping; token accounting currently attributes per-connection tokens, leading to double-counting when connections reuse.
- Rate-limiter config on the dedicated pool has a conservative burst bucket with no route exemptions for internal telemetry.
Repro attempts:
- SRE reproduced similar token-drain pattern by simulating 200 mock keepalive websockets behind 4 NAT addresses.
- Lowering simulated heartbeat frequency to 300s prevented burst exhaustion in tests.
Open questions:
- Can customer modify heartbeat cadence? (customer prefers 30s to keep telemetry fresh)
- Can we exempt internal telemetry route or mark it as lightweight so it doesn't draw from tenant burst credits?
- Is there an upstream fix to dedupe token accounting for multiplexed NAT mappings?
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks for the report — triaging this now. I've pulled ratecontrol graphs for tenant sv-001 and see repeated small drains matching your keepalive cadence. Can you confirm how many distinct outbound IPs your workers use?

2026-03-10 09:45 - Customer (ScaleVector - ops@scalevector.com): We have a pool of 4 NAT IPs for egress. Workers are 220 total across k8s. Heartbeat sends are to /v1/streams with a 30s interval. We can tolerate 2 minute cadence if needed, but do prefer 30s for internal latency metrics.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally by simulating 200 websocket clients behind 4 IPs. Confirmed account-bucket drains due to per-request counting. Suggest two mitigation paths: (1) short-term: increase tenant burst capacity or create a route exemption for telemetry, (2) medium-term: change rate-limiter accounting to consider keepalive heartbeat header and not count as full token consumption. Filed related PR(s).

2026-03-11 14:22 - Support (Marta Ruiz): We've scoped a targeted patch to allow route-level quota-exempt flag for internal agent endpoints; rolling a canary to staging edge-proxy. Customer asked for step-by-step on how to switch telemetry to an exempt route if they can update agent config.
2026-03-12 08:37 - Customer: We'll trial increasing keepalive interval to 120s tonight and will monitor. Please provide the recommended config for exempt route and any risks.

2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Provided mitigation steps and PR references. Noted risk: exempting routes increases load that bypasses tenant-level throttles — recommend applying only to authenticated internal agent client IDs and within dedicated pool settings.
resolution_notes:
Workaround provided: customer will change keepalive cadence to 120s for immediate relief.
Short-term fix: Support/SRE created a temporary route-exempt profile for the customer's agent client_id; applied as a canary to 2 edge nodes (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/119). Monitor rolling.
Medium-term fix: ratecontrol team is implementing dedupe logic for NAT-multiplexed websocket accounting and a header-based lightweight-check to mark telemetry pings as non-burst-bearing (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ratecontrol/pull/842). Planned rollout: canary -> staged -> full over 2 weeks.
Follow-ups:
- Post-deployment verification: confirm no tenant 429s during next 7 nightly cycles.
- Add runbook entry describing telemetry exemption policy and how customers request exemptions for edge agents.
- Product decision: document recommended keepalive cadence for dedicated pools.
